# 1 Kings Chapter 16 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** The word of the LORD came to Jehu son of Hanani with a message for Baasha:

**2** "I lifted you out of the dust and made you leader of my people Israel. But you have followed in Jeroboam's footsteps. You have led my people Israel into sin, provoking me with their sins.

**3** So I am going to consume Baasha and his family. I will make your house like the house of Jeroboam son of Nebat.

**4** Dogs will eat any of Baasha's family who die in the city, and vultures will eat any who die in the countryside."

**5** The rest of Baasha's reign — what he did and his military accomplishments — is recorded in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel.

**6** Baasha died and was buried in Tirzah. His son Elah succeeded him.

**7** The LORD's message through the prophet Jehu son of Hanani was directed against Baasha and his house both because of all the evil he had done in the LORD's sight, provoking him with his actions (just like the house of Jeroboam), and because he had destroyed it.

**8** In the twenty-sixth year of King Asa of Judah, Elah son of Baasha became king of Israel in Tirzah. He reigned two years.

**9** His officer Zimri, commander of half the chariot force, plotted against him. While Elah was in Tirzah, getting drunk at the home of Arza, his palace manager,

**10** Zimri came in, struck him down, and killed him. This was in the twenty-seventh year of King Asa of Judah. Zimri then took the throne.

**11** As soon as he was seated on the throne, he killed off Baasha's entire family. He didn't spare a single male — relative or friend.

**12** Zimri wiped out the entire house of Baasha, just as the LORD had declared through the prophet Jehu —

**13** because of all the sins Baasha and his son Elah committed and caused Israel to commit, provoking the LORD, the God of Israel, with their worthless idols.

**14** The rest of Elah's reign and everything he did are recorded in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel.

**15** In the twenty-seventh year of King Asa of Judah, Zimri reigned in Tirzah — for seven days. The Israelite army was besieging the Philistine town of Gibbethon at the time.

**16** When the troops in the field heard that Zimri had conspired and assassinated the king, they proclaimed Omri, the army commander, king of Israel right there in the camp.

**17** Omri marched up from Gibbethon with all Israel and laid siege to Tirzah.

**18** When Zimri saw the city was lost, he went into the fortified section of the royal palace and set the palace on fire around himself. He died in the flames —

**19** because of the sins he had committed, doing evil in the LORD's sight and walking in the ways of Jeroboam and in the sin Jeroboam had caused Israel to commit.

**20** The rest of Zimri's reign and his conspiracy are recorded in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel.

**21** Then Israel split into two factions: half supported Tibni son of Ginath for king, and half supported Omri.

**22** Omri's supporters defeated Tibni's. Tibni died, and Omri became king.

**23** In the thirty-first year of King Asa of Judah, Omri became king of Israel. He reigned twelve years, six of them in Tirzah.

**24** He bought the hill of Samaria from Shemer for two talents of silver, built a city on it, and named it Samaria after Shemer, the former owner.

**25** Omri did evil in the LORD's sight — worse than any king before him.

**26** He walked in all the ways of Jeroboam son of Nebat and in the sin Jeroboam had caused Israel to commit, provoking the LORD, the God of Israel, with worthless idols.

**27** The rest of Omri's reign, his accomplishments, and his military exploits are recorded in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel.

**28** Omri died and was buried in Samaria. His son Ahab succeeded him.

**29** Ahab son of Omri became king of Israel in the thirty-eighth year of King Asa of Judah. He reigned in Samaria for twenty-two years.

**30** Ahab son of Omri did more evil in the LORD's sight than any king before him.

**31** As if it weren't enough to commit the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, he married Jezebel daughter of King Ethbaal of Sidon and began to serve and worship Baal.

**32** He built a temple for Baal in Samaria and set up an altar in it.

**33** Ahab also set up an Asherah pole. He did more to provoke the LORD, the God of Israel, than all the kings of Israel before him.

**34** During Ahab's reign, Hiel of Bethel rebuilt Jericho. Laying its foundations cost him his firstborn son Abiram, and setting up its gates cost him his youngest son Segub — exactly as the LORD had declared through Joshua son of Nun.

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

1. **16:9 — "getting drunk"**: Elah dies the way he lived — drunk at a party. The narrator wastes no sympathy on him. Two years of reign, two verses of description, and an assassination during a binge.
2. **16:15-18 — Zimri's seven days**: The shortest reign in Israelite history. Zimri's entire monarchy fits into a week, ending in self-inflicted fire. It reads like a dark comedy of political violence.
3. **16:24 — Samaria**: The most consequential real estate transaction in northern kingdom history. Omri buys a hill and builds a capital that will stand until the Assyrians destroy it 150 years later. Politically, Omri is one of Israel's most significant kings — but the narrator gives him four verses.
4. **16:31 — Jezebel**: The single most destructive marriage in the Hebrew Bible. Ahab's alliance with Sidon through Jezebel doesn't just introduce foreign worship — it brings organized, state-sponsored Baal worship backed by royal power and prophetic persecution.
5. **16:34 — the cost of disobedience**: A man rebuilds a cursed city and loses his sons — the fulfillment of a curse spoken by Joshua centuries earlier. The Bible has a long memory.

— PNEUMA
